target_customer: Technical artists, environment artists and game or VFX studios that author PBR materials and textures
problem: Authoring procedural materials is slow and specialist work, and sharing material graphs between artists and tools is awkward.
business_model: Software subscription for a browser-based procedural material engine and editor (pricing not found; early access)
product_category: Procedural material and texture authoring tool

founders.name: Matthew Turnshek
founders.background_notes: Solo founder per the YC page, which lists no education or prior employers.

competitors.name: Material Maker
competitors.what: Free open source procedural material and texture generator built on the Godot engine
competitors.traction_then: Version 1.0 reported released; adoption figures not found

technical_complexity.rationale: A GPU shader node graph engine running in the browser is substantial but achievable for one strong engineer; the AI agent layer came later.

defensibility.rationale: Established tools such as Substance Designer and free tools such as Material Maker exist; lock-in from authored graphs is modest.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Aqueduct found; incumbent products named from alternatives listings, undated.

market_need_then: Game and VFX studios use procedural materials widely, and incumbents are subscription priced; the company's own pitch is browser sharing and agent-friendly graphs. No independent demand data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short and direct with calls to action such as Open Aqueduct and Get Early Access

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand assets found; aqueduct is a common word shared with unrelated software, so search visibility is poor.

outcome_analysis: Aqueduct is a one person company that remains active, now offering a browser procedural material engine with an MCP server so AI agents can build materials. No funding announcement, exit, shutdown or traction numbers were found, so the outcome is undetermined and the data suggests a small, bootstrapped or lightly funded effort.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights reports about $500K total as a convertible note under the name Iliad; no primary source, so no round is recorded. Search summaries show the YC page slug iliad now resolves to the Aqueduct page, suggesting an earlier name Iliad (earlier product was a game asset generator per a YC launch snippet), but no rename source or date was found, so no rebrand is recorded. Founder education and employers not found. Completeness pass: Round recorded (convertible note, about $500K) rests on a single database, CB Insights, under the name Iliad; no date given.
